readings.title: Valuation of Persons
readings.subtitle: Vows of Dedication
readings.text: [Leviticus 27:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When a man separates a vow, by your evaluation of lives unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [3] <dq>when your evaluation is of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old, then your evaluation shall be fifty sheqels of silver, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And if it is a female, then your evaluation shall be thirty sheqels;</dq> [5] <dq>and if from five years old up to twenty years old, then your evaluation for a male shall be twenty sheqels, and for a female ten sheqels;</dq> [6] <dq>and if from a month old up to five years old, then your evaluation for a male shall be five sheqels of silver, and for a female your evaluation shall be three sheqels of silver;</dq> [7] <dq>and if from sixty years old and above, if it is a male, then your evaluation shall be fifteen sheqels, and for a female ten sheqels.</dq> [8] <dq>‘But if he is too poor to pay your evaluation, then he shall present himself before the priest, and the priest shall set a value for him. According to the ability of him who vowed, the priest shall value him.</dq>

readings.title: Valuation of Beasts
readings.subtitle: Clean and Unclean Animals
readings.text: [Leviticus 27:9] <dq>‘And if it is a beast of which they bring an offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all such given to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is set-apart.</dq> [10] <dq>‘He is not to replace it or exchange it, good for spoilt or spoilt for good. And if he at all exchanges beast for beast, then both it and the one exchanged for it is set-apart.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And if it is any unclean beast of which they do not bring an offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then he shall present the beast before the priest;</dq> [12] <dq>and the priest shall value it, whether it is good or spoilt. According to your evaluation, O priest, so it shall be.</dq> [13] <dq>‘But if he indeed redeems it, then he shall add one-fifth to your evaluation.</dq>

readings.title: Valuation of Property
readings.subtitle: Houses and Fields
readings.text: [Leviticus 27:14] <dq>‘And when a man sets his house apart, to be set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then the priest shall value it, whether it is good or spoilt. As the priest values it, so it stands.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And if he who sets it apart does redeem his house, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of your evaluation to it, and it shall be his.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And if a man sets apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a field he owns, then your evaluation shall be according to the seed for it – a ḥomer of barley seed at fifty sheqels of silver.</dq> [17] <dq>‘If he sets his field apart from the Year of Yoḇel, according to your evaluation it stands.</dq> [18] <dq>‘But if he sets his field apart after the Yoḇel, then the priest shall reckon to him the silver due according to the years that remain till the Year of Yoḇel, and it shall be deducted from your evaluation.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And if he who sets the field apart ever wishes to redeem it, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of your evaluation to it, and it shall be his.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it is no longer redeemed,</dq> [21] <dq>but the field, when it is released in the Yoḇel, shall be set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as a field under the ban. It becomes the possession of the priest.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And if a man sets apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a field which he has bought, which is not the field of his possession,</dq> [23] <dq>then the priest shall reckon to him the amount of your evaluation, up to the Year of Yoḇel, and he shall give your evaluation on that day, set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [24] <dq>‘In the Year of Yoḇel the field returns to him from whom he bought it, to him whose is the possession of the land.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And all your evaluations are to be according to the sheqel of the set-apart place: twenty gĕrahs to the sheqel.</dq>

readings.title: Firstlings and Devoted Things
readings.subtitle: Irredeemable Offerings
readings.text: [Leviticus 27:26] <dq>‘However, a first-born among beasts, which is first-born to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, no man sets it apart, whether ox or sheep – it is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>’s.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if among the unclean beasts, then he shall ransom it according to your evaluation, and shall add one-fifth to it. And if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your evaluation.</dq> [28] <dq>‘However, whatever a man lays under ban for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of all that he has, man and beast, or the field of his possession, is not sold or redeemed. Whatever is laid under ban is most set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>‘No one under the ban, under the ban among men, is ransomed, but shall certainly be put to death.</dq>

readings.title: The Tithe
readings.subtitle: Conclusion of Leviticus
readings.text: [Leviticus 27:30] <dq>‘And all the tithe of the land – of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree – belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>‘If a man indeed redeems any of his tithes, he adds one-fifth to it.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And the entire tithe of the herd and of the flock, all that passes under the rod, the tenth one is set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [33] <dq>‘He does not inquire whether it is good or spoilt, nor does he exchange it. And if he exchanges it at all, then both it and the one exchanged for it are set-apart, it is not redeemed.’ ”</dq> [34] These are the commands which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh for the children of Yisra’ĕl on Mount Sinai.

readings.title: The Command at Sinai
readings.subtitle: Numbering the Armies
readings.text: [Numbers 1:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Appointment, on the first day of the second new moon, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Mitsrayim, saying, [2] <dq>“Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, by their clans, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, every male, head by head,</dq> [3] <dq>from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army in Yisra’ĕl. Number them by their divisions, you and Aharon.</dq> [4] <dq>“And with you there is to be a man from every tribe, each one the head of his father’s house.</dq>

readings.title: The Heads of the Tribes
readings.subtitle: Leaders of the Thousands
readings.text: [Numbers 1:5] <dq>“And these are the names of the men who stand with you: from Re’uḇĕn, Eli’tsur son of Shede’ur;</dq> [6] <dq>from Shim‛on, Shelumi’ĕl son of Tsurishaddai;</dq> [7] <dq>from Yehuḏah, Naḥshon son of Amminaḏaḇ;</dq> [8] <dq>from Yissasḵar, Nethan’ĕl son of Tsu‛ar;</dq> [9] <dq>from Zeḇulun, Eli’aḇ son of Ḥĕlon;</dq> [10] <dq>from the sons of Yosĕph: from Ephrayim, Elishama son of Ammihuḏ; from Menashsheh, Gamli’ĕl son of Peḏahtsur;</dq> [11] <dq>from Binyamin, Aḇiḏan son of Giḏ‛oni;</dq> [12] <dq>from Dan, Aḥi‛ezer son of Ammishaddai;</dq> [13] <dq>from Ashĕr, Paḡ’i’ĕl son of Oḵran;</dq> [14] <dq>from Gaḏ, Elyasaph son of Deu’ĕl;</dq> [15] <dq>from Naphtali, Aḥira son of Ěnan.”</dq> [16] These were the called ones of the congregation, leaders of the tribes of their fathers, heads of the thousands of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Assembly
readings.subtitle: Declaration of Lineage
readings.text: [Numbers 1:17] And Mosheh and Aharon took these men who were called by name, [18] and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second new moon. And they declared their ancestry by their clans, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, head by head. [19] As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh, so he registered them in the Wilderness of Sinai.

readings.title: Census: Reuben, Simeon, Gad
readings.subtitle: The South Camp
readings.text: [Numbers 1:20] And the children of Re’uḇĕn, Yisra’ĕl’s first-born, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, every male head by head, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [21] those who were registered of the tribe of Re’uḇĕn were forty-six thousand five hundred. [22] From the children of Shim‛on, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, of those who were registered, according to the number of names, every male head by head, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [23] those who were registered of the tribe of Shim‛on were fifty-nine thousand three hundred. [24] From the children of Gaḏ, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [25] those who were registered of the tribe of Gaḏ were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

readings.title: Census: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun
readings.subtitle: The East Camp
readings.text: [Numbers 1:26] From the children of Yehuḏah, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [27] those who were registered of the tribe of Yehuḏah were seventy-four thousand six hundred. [28] From the children of Yissasḵar, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [29] those who were registered of the tribe of Yissasḵar were fifty-four thousand four hundred. [30] From the children of Zeḇulun, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [31] those who were registered of the tribe of Zeḇulun were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

readings.title: Census: Ephraim, Manasseh, Benjamin
readings.subtitle: The West Camp
readings.text: [Numbers 1:32] From the sons of Yosĕph: the children of Ephrayim, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [33] those who were registered of the tribe of Ephrayim were forty thousand five hundred. [34] From the children of Menashsheh, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [35] those who were registered of the tribe of Menashsheh were thirty-two thousand two hundred. [36] From the children of Binyamin, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [37] those who were registered of the tribe of Binyamin were thirty-five thousand four hundred.

readings.title: Census: Dan, Asher, Naphtali
readings.subtitle: The North Camp
readings.text: [Numbers 1:38] From the children of Dan, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [39] those who were registered of the tribe of Dan were sixty-two thousand seven hundred. [40] From the children of Ashĕr, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [41] those who were registered of the tribe of Ashĕr were forty-one thousand five hundred. [42] From the children of Naphtali, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army, [43] those who were registered of the tribe of Naphtali were fifty-three thousand four hundred.

readings.title: The Grand Total
readings.subtitle: 603,550 Men of War
readings.text: [Numbers 1:44] These were those registered, whom Mosheh and Aharon registered, with the leaders of Yisra’ĕl, twelve men, each one for his father’s house. [45] And all those registered of the children of Yisra’ĕl, by their fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army in Yisra’ĕl, [46] all those registered were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

readings.title: The Levite Exemption
readings.subtitle: Guardians of the Dwelling Place
readings.text: [Numbers 1:47] But the Lĕwites were not registered among them by their fathers’ tribe, [48] because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Mosheh, saying, [49] <dq>“Only the tribe of Lĕwi you do not register, nor take a census of them among the children of Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [50] <dq>“Instead, appoint the Lĕwites over the Dwelling Place of the Witness, over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They bear the Dwelling Place and all its furnishings, and they attend to it, and camp around the Dwelling Place.</dq> [51] <dq>“And when the Dwelling Place is to go forward, the Lĕwites take it down. And when the Dwelling Place is to be set up, the Lĕwites set it up. And the stranger who comes near is put to death.</dq> [52] <dq>“And the children of Yisra’ĕl shall pitch their tents, everyone by his own camp, everyone by his own banner, according to their divisions,”</dq> [53] <dq>but let the Lĕwites camp around the Dwelling Place of the Witness, so that there be no wrath on the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl. And the Lĕwites shall guard the duty of the Dwelling Place of the Witness.”</dq> [54] And the children of Yisra’ĕl did according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh, so they did.
